newsitem.title: ITALY: Police arrest 22 in anti-terrorism swoop in Italy.
newsitem.headline: Police arrest 22 in anti-terrorism swoop in Italy.

text.p: Police said they had arrested 22 people in raids across Italy on Thursday on suspicion of supplying arms, false documents and other support to Algeria's radical Armed Islamic Group (GIA).

Investigators in the northwest city of Turin, from where the operation was spearheaded after a year of surveillance, said they believed the suspects may have supplied logistical support for fatal bomb attacks last year in France.

The 22, all Arabs and almost all of them Algerians, were held in police raids on homes and meeting places of North African immigrants in at least eight cities in Italy, including Milan, Turin, Rome and Naples.
"At the moment we do not believe that the organisation was planning to carry out attacks in Italy," Turin prosecutor Maurizio Laudi told a news conference.
"However, we do believe that the people arrested played a logistics role in terrorist actions that have happened in France, such as the bomb attack on the Paris metro," Laudi said.
A gas-canister bomb exploded in July 1995 on a rush-hour underground train at the crowded Saint-Michel metro station in Paris, killing eight people.
The attack was the first of eight bombings and attempted bombings in France which authorities there have blamed on Algerian Moslem extremists.

The GIA, fighting to establish a purist fundamentalist state in Algeria, is blamed for killing civilians, including women activists, writers, journalists and religious workers in a five-year-old conflict with the Algerian government.
Thursday's raids, under an operation codenamed Shabka, the Arabic for net, involved some 300 police and followed lengthy surveillance and telephone taps.
Forces in France, Belgium, Britain and Germany cooperated in enquiries leading up to the swoop, staged at some 60 different addresses, police said.
Premises searched included an Islamic centre in Milan and two mosques in Turin, though police said no one in an official position at the three sites was suspected of any offence.
Several suspected GIA supporters were arrested in Italy last year in a similar operation to Thursday's.

Police said the people held in the latest raids were suspected of supplying arms and false documents to the GIA as well as smuggling activists into Europe, gathering funds and arranging safe houses for fugitives.

The arrest warrant, quoted by the Italian news agency ANSA, said the suspects were believed to belong to a "criminal association of the GIA active in several regions of Italy in direct operational contact with similar groups operating in other European states and in Algeria".
More than 50,000 people have died in Algeria's violence since early 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election in which radical Islamists had taken a huge lead.
